summary.tagline: The Teufelshöhle is a natural karst cave near the Upper Franconian city of Pottenstein in the district of Bayr

days.title: Main Show Caves and Entrances
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Kuppelsaal
stops.detail: The Kuppelsaal, which was known as the Great Teufelsloch before the development, has a height of more than ten meters with a floor area of about 100 square meters; a 15-meter-thick rock ceiling lies above it.

stops.name: Barbarossadom
stops.detail: The Barbarossadom is about 45 meters long, 18 meters wide and up to 18 meters high, with an overlying rock ceiling 52 meters thick.

days.title: Great Halls and Giant Formations
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Riesensaal
stops.detail: The Riesensaal, the largest room in the Teufelshöhle, is about 30 meters long, 16 meters wide and 13 meters high, with 45 meters of rock above it.

stops.name: Kleine Teufelshöhle
stops.detail: In the cave register of the Franconian Alb, with over 3,500 caves over an area of 6,400 square kilometers, the Teufelshöhle is registered as D 95 and the Kleine Teufelshöhle as D 148.

days.title: Connected Systems and Southern Gorges
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM start, after checking official access hours

stops.name: Brennnesselbau
stops.detail: Connected to this is the Brennnesselbau, which has an excavated exit towards the valley side.

stops.name: Zankenhöhle
stops.detail: The Brennnesselbau is also connected to the Zankenhöhle.

stops.name: Teufelsschlucht
stops.detail: The Teufelsschlucht located to the south was connected to the Lehmhöhle, the entrance of which has collapsed.
